key_insight: Including solute mass transfer in alloy droplet impact simulations changes the predicted solidification dynamics and reveals where macrosegregation forms during splat spreading and freezing.
engineering_relevance: The model improves prediction of solidifying alloy splats, which is important for controlling defects such as cracking in thermal spray and additive manufacturing processes.
method: Fully coupled multiphysics simulation of multiphase hydrodynamics, wetting, conjugate heat transfer, phase change, and mass transfer
Concentration-flux-correction algorithm to conserve solute mass at the discretization level
Validation against several benchmarks before applying the model to an alloy droplet impact case
evidence_signal: The abstract reports careful benchmark validation and shows improved agreement with experimental observations when mass transfer and solute transport are included.
watch_item: Results depend on accurate mushy-zone thickness and solute transport modeling, so implementation details can strongly affect predicted segregation patterns.
paper_title: Numerical Modeling of a Metallic Alloy Droplet Impact, Solidification, and Macrosegregation
